origin.description: Finds a root by calling the one-dimensional steady-state solver.
origin.usage: multiroot.1D(f, start, maxiter = 100, nspec = NULL, dimens = NULL, ...)

arguments.name: nspec
arguments.text: Number of species. One species uses a banded Jacobian.

origin.details: The state is passed to steady.1D with method stode.
origin.value: A list with root, f.root, iter, and estim.precis.
origin.example:
f <- function(x) c(x[2] - x[1], x[1] - 2 * x[2] + x[3], 1 - x[3])
multiroot.1D(f, rep(0.2, 3), nspec = 1)

translation.description: Finds a root by calling the one-dimensional steady-state solver.

arguments.name: nspec
arguments.text: Number of species. One species uses a banded Jacobian.

translation.details: The state is passed to steady.1D with method stode.
translation.value: A list with root, f.root, iter, and estim.precis.
translation.example:
from rootSolve import multiroot_1d

def f(x):
    return [x[1] - x[0], x[0] - 2 * x[1] + x[2], 1 - x[2]]

print(multiroot_1d(f, [0.2, 0.2, 0.2], nspec=1))
